strings: A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
All engineering related spawners go here
Automagically transforms into a random arcade machine. If you see this while in a shift, please create a bug report.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
An old, deactivated cyborg. Whilst once actively used to guard against intruders, it now simply intimidates them with its cold, steely gaze.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
A high-capacity superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
A large briefcase with a digital locking system.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
Used to monitor the station's atmospherics sensors.
A vending machine which dispenses hot drinks.
It's Sergeant-At-Armsky! He's a disgruntled assistant to the warden that would probably shoot you if he had hands.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A large beaker. Can hold up to 120 units.
A beaker. It can hold up to 60 units.
The HS-452. Installed in the 2550s by the Nanotrasen Hygiene Division, now with 2560 lead compliance! Passively replenishes itself with water when not in use.
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
A vending machine which vends food, as required by section 47-C of the NT's Prisoner Ethical Treatment Agreement.
Store your trophies of accomplishment in here, and they will stay forever.
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
Used for sweeping, and flying into the night while cackling. Black cat not included.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
Contains blood used for transfusion. Must be attached to an IV drip.
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
It's used for removing weeds or scratching your back.
A very sharp axe blade upon a short fibremetal handle. It has a long history of chopping things, but now it is used for chopping wood.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
An underfloor disposal pipe with a sorting mechanism.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
Damn, they better have the /tg/ channel on these things.
Learn skills with only minimal chance for brain damage.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
Looks like someone threw it out. Covered in donut crumbs.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
Ding-aling ding dong. Get your Nanotrasen-approved ice cream!
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
It's a storage unit for standard-issue Nanotrasen attire.
This box is shaped on the inside so that only light tubes and bulbs fit.
A basic handheld radio that communicates with local telecommunication networks.
A coil of insulated power cable.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
Used to modify prisoner IDs, as well as manage security implants placed inside convicts and parolees.
Used to view and edit personnel's security records.
A computer used for remotely handling slimes.
A rich patch of dirt, usually used in gardens.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
A soft and fluffy pillow. You can smack someone with this!
A one-way air valve that does not require power. Passes gas when the output pressure is lower than the target pressure.
A sign that warns of high-power testing equipment in the area.
Bluespace technologies on the application of bureaucracy.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
Used to monitor active health sensors built into most of the crew's uniforms.
A simple bowl, used for soups and salads.
Pstttthhh! Pass it under the table.
Really takes you back to highschool lunch.
It has a picture of drinking glasses on it.
Just be careful your food doesn't melt the spoon first.
A very safe, barely sharp knife made of plastic. Good for cutting food and not much else.
A cheap metal tray to pile today's meal onto.
Used to keep bodies in until someone fetches them. Includes a high-tech alert system.
Automagically transforms into a random cola vendor. If you see this while in a shift, please create a bug report.

A guide to the exhibit, explaining how recent developments in mindshield implant and cloning technologies by Nanotrasen Corporation have led to the development and the effective immortality of the 'perfect man', the loyal Nanotrasen Employee.
A remote control switch for the combustion chamber's igniter.
A large piece of equipment used to open a window into the subspace dimension.
A compact micro-machine capable of amplifying weak subspace transmissions.
Some rods. Can be used for building or something.
Used to build digital clocks, just secure to the wall.
Control exploration drones from interstellar distances. Communication lag not included.
Thick, tough flooring created with multiple layers of metal.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
For the exotic art of paper shuffling.
You probably shouldn't be holding this.
It's black and greasy. Looks like Beepsky made another mess.
Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the most robust of them all?
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
It's a burial receptacle for the dearly departed.
A warning sign which reads 'NO SMOKING'.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
A pump for cycling an external airlock controlled by the connected doors.
Accepts boulders and refines non-metallic ores into sheets using internal chemicals.
Fill it with water, but don't forget a mop!
The world of janitalia wouldn't be complete without a mop.
A rubber stamp for stamping important documents.
A suit that completely restrains the wearer. Manufactured by Antyphun Corp.
A roll of elastic cloth, perfect for stabilizing all kinds of wounds, from cuts and burns, to broken bones.
A bacteriostatic mesh used to dress burns.
Basic sterile sutures used to seal up cuts and lacerations and stop bleeding.

Several lumps of snow put together to form a snowman.
Traditional burial garments from the early 22nd century.

A heavy, metal trashcart with wheels.

Used to set the destination of properly wrapped packages.

These seeds grow into apple trees.

It has pictures of pill bottles on its front.
A computer to remotely control a gas turbine.

Used for watching the AI and the RD's goons from the safety of his office.

A vending machine stocked with a multitude of security outfits, including standardized uniforms and general equipment.
A figurine depicting Ian the corgi! HoP's goodest boy.
These clunky gauntlets allow you to drag things with more confidence on them not getting nabbed from you.

An old handheld radio. You could use it, if you really wanted to.
A telescreen that connects to the turbine's camera.
A sign labelling an area containing chemical equipment.

Don't shine it in your eyes!
A brave security cyborg gave its life to help you look like a complete tool.
Drymate brand monkey cubes. Just add water!
An entire book on how to not turn yourself into a fly mutant.
There's little more you could want from a cigar.

The height of fashion, and they're pre-polished!

Uses shearing action and growth inducers to reshape your coworkers external features!

A sign labelling an area where scientific data is stored.

A stylish vendor to dispense the most stylish bar clothing!
A vending machine renowned for vending industrial grade clothing.
Get a load, or give, of these all natural Xenos!
To be issued to those authorized to act as deputy of security.
A poster encouraging the swift reporting of crime or seditious behavior to station security.
A rectangular steel crate. It seems to be painted to look like gold.
A simple microscope, allowing you to examine micro-organisms.
A premium single-malt whiskey, gently matured inside the tunnels of a nuclear shelter. TUNNEL WHISKEY RULES.
For when you get a bad case of the space blues.
Used to monitor the crew's PDA messages, as well as request console messages.
A metal tray to lay food on.
Used to access the various cameras on the labor camp.
A telescreen that connects to the auxiliary base's camera.

A terrible, terrible thing. It's really awful!

A device that draws power from bluespace and creates a permanent tracking beacon.
A machine used for recycling dead monkeys into monkey cubes.
Human friendly interface to the mysterious gate next to it.
You get the feeling someone might have been hanged in these boots.
Ashes to ashes, dust to dust, and into space.
He stared into the void and listened. He didn't expect an answer...
A plushie depicting an adorable mothperson. It's a huggable bug!
Aah, vodka. Prime choice of drink AND fuel by Russians worldwide.
Contains all the paper you'll never need, IN COLOR!
